result.summary: Project invitation tokens now expire one week after they are issued, the same period as project transfer tokens. One helper, generate_invitation_token() in taiga/projects/services/invitations.py, returns the token and its expiration date together. Every issuer uses it: membership create, bulk create, project import and sample_data. Only pending invitations with token_expires_at in the future are accepted. Expired tokens and old tokens with no expiration date return 404 on GET /invitations/<token>, on login with invitation_token and on private register, and the invitation is not accepted (on register, no user is created). Resending an invitation gives it a new token and a new expiration date, so the old link stops working. I also made token and token_expires_at read-only in MembershipValidator: before this, an API client could choose its own token or a longer expiration date. Factories now set token_expires_at to now + 7 days. Tests: the related files pass (155) and make check-fast passes (238). The full suite (make test) gave 1752 passed and 9 failed. The 9 failures are logo and avatar upload tests that failed with FileNotFoundError. All 9 passed when I reran them on their own, so they are probably a test-isolation problem with media files, not caused by this change. I did not confirm this in a clean environment. I could not show that the new tests fail on the old code: the command to revert and rerun them was blocked.

changes.summary: Added INVITATION_TOKEN_LIFETIME (7 days), generate_invitation_token(), set_invitation_token(), rotate_invitation_token() and valid_invitations_queryset(). get_membership_by_token() now rejects expired tokens and tokens with no expiration date.
Bulk invitations set the token and token_expires_at through the helper. Removed the unused uuid import.
pre_save sets the token through the helper. resend_invitation rotates the token before it sends the email. InvitationViewSet.get_queryset only returns invitations that have not expired.
token and token_expires_at are now read-only in MembershipValidator.
Imported memberships get the token and expiration date from the helper. Removed the unused uuid import.
Sample invitations use the helper, so they have a valid expiration date.
MembershipFactory and InvitationFactory set token_expires_at to now + 7 days.

Tests for: the helper, create and bulk create setting the expiration date (client values are ignored), resend changing the token (old link 404, new link 200), and GET by token for a valid, an expired and an old token.
Tests that login and private register reject expired and old invitation tokens with 404 and accept nothing. Added a test that private register works with a valid invitation.
Test that an imported invitation gets a token valid for one week and that an expiration date in the import data is ignored.
Added a 2026-11-02 entry for this change.

acceptance.criterion: Expired and legacy invitation tokens are rejected everywhere (GET invitation, login, register)
acceptance.evidence: test_get_invitation_by_expired_or_legacy_token_returns_404, test_get_auth_token_with_expired_or_legacy_invitation_is_rejected and test_private_register_with_expired_or_legacy_invitation_is_rejected pass, each for both the expired case and the no-date case.

acceptance.criterion: Resending gives a new valid token and the old one stops working
acceptance.evidence: test_api_resend_invitation_rotates_token: the token changes, the expiration date is now + 7 days, the email contains the new token, the old token returns 404 and the new one returns 200.

acceptance.criterion: Every issuer sets the token and its expiration date through one shared helper
acceptance.evidence: The API create, bulk create, import and sample_data all use generate_invitation_token or set_invitation_token. Covered by the create, bulk create and import tests.

acceptance.criterion: Factories create invitations that expire one week from now
acceptance.evidence: tests/factories.py: token_expires_at = LazyFunction(now + 7 days) on MembershipFactory and InvitationFactory.

acceptance.criterion: The change is covered by tests
acceptance.evidence: pytest on test_memberships.py, test_auth.py and test_importer_api.py: 155 passed. I could not confirm that the new tests fail on the old code, because the revert-and-rerun command was blocked.

acceptance.criterion: The existing test suite still passes
acceptance.evidence: make check-fast passes (238). make test: 1752 passed, 9 failed. The 9 failures are avatar and logo upload tests (FileNotFoundError on media files) and all 9 passed when I reran them on their own (pytest -k 'avatar or logo': 9 passed). They look like a test-isolation problem not caused by this change, but I did not confirm this in a clean environment or CI.

human_needed.question: When this is deployed, all pending invitations sent before it stop working because they have no expiration date. Is this acceptable, or should a data migration give them a grace period (for example now + 7 days)?
human_needed.why: The task says to treat old tokens as expired. Without a migration, admins must resend every pending invitation after the deploy.

human_needed.question: Is it acceptable that token and token_expires_at can no longer be set through the memberships API?
human_needed.why: Before this change, a client could send its own token. That would bypass the one-week limit, so I made both fields read-only. This changes the API for any client that relied on it.

human_needed.question: Do the 9 avatar and logo upload tests also fail in a full run without this change (in CI or a clean environment)?
human_needed.why: They failed only in the long full run and passed on their own. They look like a test-isolation problem with media files, but I could not run the suite on the old code to confirm.

harness_used: AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md: commands (make check-fast, make test, make db-up), single-file pytest commands, the --create-db advice, conventions and the instruction to add a log entry
docs/harness/log.md: format for the new entry
make db-up and the compose PostgreSQL for the integration tests
make check-fast as the fast gate

harness_gaps.problem: In the full make test run, 9 avatar and logo upload tests fail with FileNotFoundError but pass when run on their own. The docs do not mention this, so it looks like a regression and costs time to investigate.
Running the full suite takes about 15 minutes, and there is no faster documented way to run only the tests that touch memberships, invitations and auth. I had to pick the test files by hand.
flake8 on a changed file shows many old violations mixed with new ones. The harness has no way to lint only the changed lines, so it is hard to prove that new code is clean.

Token lifetimes are not documented. The transfer token period is hard-coded in taiga/projects/services/transfer.py, and the password recovery period is a setting. Nothing in the docs describes how long tokens are valid.
